questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather, the beach, the different culture, the language, and the lower cost of living there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The city is really pretty, the weather is almost always nice, the culture is interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, but some stuff especially for choosing courses was difficult to find information about, such as course descriptions, timetables and such.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a mentor that i could text if i had any doubts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The best is to look on Facebook Erasmus groups for the city, or Whatsapp groups. Also Erasmus Life Valencia offers housing (look at their website).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For Valencia, if you want to live in a student are, choose to live in or close to Blasco Ibanez instead of the city center. In this area there are so many students, bars, restaurents, supermarkets and such, and also its really close to the universities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find some info, because some is just in spanish but overall it was okay.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can email their international office and they respond pretty quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes i wanted but a lot of them are just in spanish so be careful and apply fast if you just want classes in english.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply fast for the courses you want, make sure they are in english if you don't speak spanish.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Classes were very easy, the level is definitely lower than at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had most BA courses and two MA courses at another faculty than mine (telecom), but all classes are pretty easy - even the MA courses are easier than most BA courses at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Its more personal compared to KU - often time the professors are at the exercise classes (labs) instead of TAs, but I experienced almost no home assignments compared to KU which has a lot of assignments to deliver throughout the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Signal and natural

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All courses were good overall.
The MA courses from the telecom faculty (Signal and natural
language processing
with deep, and Reinforcement Learning) were interesting but pretty easy and almost no home assignments.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Now that I look at my bank I am shocked at how much money I spent food every month as well as on myself. You can definitely do that cheaper.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I mean everything is cheaper than in Denmark which I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UPV has free sports, gym, dance classes and so on which is really good

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the free sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to day-trips to small cities outside Valencia, go to Morocco, go to Andalucia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Its not that different from Denmark after all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I almost only met other Erasmus students - because I dont speak Spanish and a lot of spanish students dont speak that well english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Shops close on sundays. But some supermarkets and cafes are still open, and most shops in the city center do not close.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendly people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably to live in Blasco Ibanez or close if you want to be with a lot of students - use the free language courses that UPV offers. Go to Erasmus activities to meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The food there is really cheap and you can get hot meals for almost no money which is really nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably to balance school and free-time - because you want to do everything but still you have to attend school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
